explanation: Push opening brackets. Each closing bracket must match the most recent unmatched opening bracket. The string is valid only if every close matches and no opens remain at the end.
timeComplexity: O(n) time. Each bracket is pushed or matched once; early rejection can stop sooner.
spaceComplexity: O(n) auxiliary space in the worst case. All n characters may be unmatched opening brackets.
attribution: JavaScript port of the independently authored EPI Practice C# algorithm; no upstream reference code copied.
correctness: The stack holds exactly the unmatched opening brackets in their nesting order. A closing bracket can legally close only the top matching type. Rejecting mismatches and requiring an empty final stack is therefore equivalent to complete proper nesting.
walkthrough: For "{[()]}()", push {, [, (, then pop them for ), ], }. The final () pushes and pops one more pair. The stack ends empty, so return true.
edgeCases: The empty bracket string is valid.
A closing bracket with an empty stack fails immediately.
Equal opening and closing counts are insufficient when types cross, as in ([)].
